item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Christmas Eve at Biltmore

turns.text: Make an 8-second widescreen history clip of Biltmore House in Asheville on Christmas Eve 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened it to family and friends. A slow exterior view is enough. Show 'Biltmore House', 'Asheville, North Carolina' and 'December 24, 1895', plus a small 'Historical reconstruction' label. Warm English narration, historically grounded rather than a fantasy castle.

item.tests: Tests geographic, architectural and period accuracy in a historical reconstruction without misrepresenting generated footage as archival evidence.

answer_sheet.Place and historical event: Biltmore House in Asheville, North Carolina, on December 24, 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened the house to family and friends.
answer_sheet.Required wording: Biltmore House; Asheville, North Carolina; December 24, 1895; Historical reconstruction.
answer_sheet.Visual treatment: A historically grounded, slow exterior view of the actual house's architecture. Lighting and camera angle are your call.
answer_sheet.People: An exterior view without people is fine; no identifiable portrayal of George Vanderbilt is needed.
answer_sheet.Voice and music: Warm English narration stating the occasion; exact wording, voice and any unobtrusive music are your call.

must_haves: The building is recognizable as Biltmore House, with its pale stone French Renaissance-style facade, steep slate roof and distinctive roofline, rather than a generic castle.
The location and date appear exactly as requested and remain readable.
A legible 'Historical reconstruction' label identifies the imagery as a reconstruction.
No modern cars, contemporary clothing, electric holiday string lights or modern visitor signage appear.
English narration identifies the opening to family and friends, not an opening to the general public.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create an 8-second widescreen historical documentary reconstruction of Biltmore House in Asheville, North Carolina on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened his home to family and friends. One continuous slow exterior establishing shot, gentle slow lateral dolly with almost imperceptible push-in, viewing the main entrance facade across the forecourt at winter dusk. Historically grounded architectural reconstruction of the actual Biltmore House designed by Richard Morris Hunt: massive French Renaissance Chateauesque limestone country house, steep slate roofs, detailed stone dormers and chimneys, asymmetrical real mansion silhouette, restrained carved stone tracery, real-world architectural proportions. NOT a medieval fortress, NOT a fantasy castle, no Disney spires, no fantastical architecture. Bare deciduous trees and subdued winter landscaping appropriate to a newly completed estate in 1895; no assumed snowfall, no modern cars, modern signage, tourists or modern infrastructure. Warm light glows discreetly through windows; modest evergreen Christmas greenery at the entrance. Refined and welcoming, natural muted winter colors, realistic limestone texture. No crowds or prominent faces; architecture is the subject. Overlay crisp legible editorial typography, exact wording: 'Biltmore House' as the main title; 'Asheville, North Carolina' underneath; 'December 24, 1895' on a third line. Keep all three readable throughout the full shot, within title-safe margins, with subtle dark backing for contrast. Small persistent bottom-right label exactly 'Historical reconstruction'. No other text. AUDIO REQUIRED: warm calm English-language documentary narrator, natural measured delivery, precisely say: 'On Christmas Eve, eighteen ninety-five, George Vanderbilt welcomed family and friends to Biltmore House.' Start narration promptly and finish within eight seconds. Soft subtle winter outdoor ambience beneath the clear narration, no competing music, no character dialogue. Historically respectful documentary mood, not fantasy spectacle.
